Links: [{"title":"Statistical Analysis of Minifilament Eruptions Using Full-disk H$\\alpha$ Blue-wing Observations at Big Bear Solar Observatory","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.20612"},{"title":"www.swsc-journal.org","url":"https://www.swsc-journal.org/10.1051/swsc/2017039"},{"title":"www.swsc-journal.org","url":"https://www.swsc-journal.org/articles/swsc/abs/2018/01/swsc170041/swsc170041.html"},{"title":"Journal of Space Weather and Space Climate (Jan 2018)","url":"https://doaj.org/article/550ca82df14048dbbd30c34b3954c85c"},{"title":"arxiv.org","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.11476"},{"title":"Sample records for coronal hole ch","url":"https://www.science.gov/topicpages/c/coronal+hole+ch"},{"title":"11institutetext: School of Physics, Trinity College Dublin, Dublin 2, Ireland","url":"https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1711.11476"},{"title":"The Observational Uncertainty of Coronal Hole Boundaries in Automated Detection Schemes","url":"https://ar5iv.arxiv.org/html/2103.14403"},{"title":"The solar origins and earth impacts of space weather","url":"https://www.tara.tcd.ie/items/05a251e9-bced-4b28-8aec-b3570d18e7ba"}]

The search found the Garton et al. (2018) paper that introduced CHIMERA, but nothing confirming that solarmonitor.org runs it in near-real time.

- **The 2018 paper:** Garton, Gallagher, and Murray published "Automated coronal hole identification via multi-thermal intensity segmentation" in the Journal of Space Weather and Space Climate, volume 8, article A02, in January 2018 ([swsc-journal.org](https://www.swsc-journal.org/10.1051/swsc/2017039)). The authors treat coronal hole segmentation as hard because holes look much like nearby quiet Sun ([doaj.org](https://doaj.org/article/550ca82df14048dbbd30c34b3954c85c)). Earlier methods generally relied on one EUV passband plus a magnetogram ([arXiv:1711.11476](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.11476)).
- **How CHIMERA works:** It analyzes the 171, 193, and 211 Å AIA channels and their intensity ratios to estimate relative temperature and density ([arxiv.org/pdf/2608.20612](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.20612)). It flags dark pixels that are cool, low-density, and unipolar in magnetic field, which screens out filament channels and quiet-Sun depressions ([same source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.20612)).
- **Later use:** A 2020s Big Bear Solar Observatory study cites CHIMERA as an automated, validated method for segmenting coronal holes ([arxiv.org/pdf/2608.20612](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.20612)). A 2021 paper on boundary uncertainty in automated detection schemes lists Garton among its authors ([ar5iv.arxiv.org/html/2103.14403](https://ar5iv.arxiv.org/html/2103.14403)).

I did not find anything on solarmonitor.org hosting CHIMERA output or on its update cadence. A targeted search on the site or its documentation would be needed to confirm that.

**Solar Synoptic Map (NOAA SWPC)**

- **Coronal holes:** Yes. Forecasters draw coronal hole boundaries as lines with hash marks on the coronal hole side. Each hole is labeled with a number, a polarity sign, and a confidence rating from 1 to 4.
- **Update cadence:** Daily. SWPC forecasters draw a new snapshot each day, and the maps have been "produced daily since then" (since June 2, 1972).
- **Archives:**
  - Official archive back to 1972: NCEI, at https://www.ngdc.noaa.gov/stp/space-weather/solar-data/solar-imagery/composites/full-sun-drawings/boulder/
  - Recent SWPC synoptic analysis maps: FTP, at ftp://ftp.swpc.noaa.gov/pub/synoptic_maps/
- **Status notes:** The page contains no outage, deprecation, or discontinuation notice for this product. The space weather conditions panel on the page shows "no data" for its readings, but that panel is separate from the synoptic map itself.

**Yes.** The page links a coronal hole product labeled "Coronal Holes," which points to:

- `./chimera.php?date=20261016` (relative path; the full URL would be `https://www.solarmonitor.org/chimera.php?date=YYYYMMDD`, assuming the site root)

**Link patterns:**
- **Coronal hole map (CHIMERA):** `chimera.php?date=YYYYMMDD`. The page shows no `type=` parameter for this product.
- **Other `type=` patterns on the page:** `full_disk.php?date=YYYYMMDD&type=<image_code>` (for example, `type=saia_00193`) and popup links such as `goes_pop.php?date=YYYYMMDD&type=xray`.

**Date-based archive access:** Yes. Pages use a `date=YYYYMMDD` parameter, and the navigation links move between dates (for example, `index.php?date=20261015` for the previous day and `index.php?date=20261009` for the previous week). The page does not show whether `chimera.php` supports dates other than the one linked.
